decisions.question: The plan says an inserted governance step runs at the root lineage. Which branch does a contract fix found during a phase land on?

options.label: The current phase branch, as its own step and commit, reaching the node and root branches through the phase's merge
options.consequence: The append-only ledger stays on one linear lineage; the fix is one identifiable commit (hsdd: S{nn} hsdd-contract ...) inside the phase's merge.

options.label: auto/v1-impl-1, then merged into the node and phase branches
options.consequence: Governance lands on the root first, as conventions picture it, but the judgement commits on two lineages would conflict in decisions.jsonl and run.jsonl at every merge.

decisions.chosen: The current phase branch, as its own step and commit, reaching the node and root branches through the phase's merge
decisions.why: Nothing runs in parallel in this run, so there is no second lineage the fix could diverge from; the conventions' reason for root-first governance (parallel phase branches reading one truth) does not arise. Keeping the ledger on one lineage avoids hand-merging an append-only file, which the planning run never had to do.
evidence: docs/auto-run/impl-execution-plan.md, Contract gaps and other governance defects

decisions.question: gate.mjs reports four errors before any step runs: its hash snapshot of the owner's files (HARNESS.md, JUDGEMENT-LAYER.md, explorer/) predates the owner's own commits a67b65a and 7a2f215. Refreshing the snapshot was refused by the session's permission classifier. How are governance steps gated?

options.label: Keep the snapshot; a step passes when it adds no gate error beyond those four, and the owner files are checked against HEAD with git diff
options.consequence: The guard keeps reporting what it reports; the comparison against HEAD is the stronger check now that the owner's files are committed. The owner can refresh the snapshot when convenient.

options.label: Refresh the snapshot anyway by another route
options.consequence: A cleaner gate output, but it works around a refusal the session's guard made, which the run does not do.

decisions.chosen: Keep the snapshot; a step passes when it adds no gate error beyond those four, and the owner files are checked against HEAD with git diff
decisions.why: The four errors are the owner's own committed edits, not a step's; git diff against HEAD shows those files unchanged (2026-10-26T17:42:43Z). Changing a guard's baseline is the owner's call once a guard has refused it.
evidence: docs/auto-run/tools/gate.mjs, owner files unchanged since the snapshot
